**Video:** [Lec 63 — NCE - Noise Contrastive Estimation](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DHBl3E0ndRA)

## Learning goals

- See why normalizing a flexible model $p_\theta(x)=u_\theta(x)/Z(\theta)$ is hard.
- State **NCE**: turn density estimation into binary classification of **data vs noise**.
- Read the logistic posterior that compares $u_\theta$ to a known noise density $p_n$.

## Before this clicks

A parametric density often has the form

$$
p_\theta(x)=\frac{u_\theta(x)}{Z(\theta)},\qquad Z(\theta)=\int u_\theta(x)\,dx.
$$

The unnormalized score $u_\theta$ may be easy; the partition function $Z(\theta)$ is often intractable. MLE needs $Z$ (or its gradient). NCE sidesteps this by never requiring an exact normalized likelihood alone — it contrasts real samples with samples from a **known noise** distribution $p_n$.

---

## Main ideas

### 1. Setup

- Data samples $x\sim p_d$ (unknown data distribution).
- Noise samples $x\sim p_n$ (you choose; easy to sample, known density).
- Mix them and ask a classifier: “did this $x$ come from data or noise?”

### 2. Posterior odds

Let prior odds of noise vs data be controlled by how many noise samples you draw (class balance). With equal mixture weight for intuition, Bayes says

$$
P(y=\mathrm{data}\mid x)=\frac{p_d(x)}{p_d(x)+p_n(x)}.
$$

NCE **models** $p_d$ by $p_\theta$ (or its unnormalized cousin) and fits $\theta$ so that a logistic classifier matching these odds works well on the mixed sample.

### 3. Logistic form with unnormalized model

Using $p_\theta(x)=u_\theta(x)/Z(\theta)$, the log-odds involve $\log u_\theta(x)-\log Z(\theta)-\log p_n(x)$. Critically, $Z(\theta)$ becomes just another parameter (or is absorbed), so you optimize a **classification** loss without integrating $u_\theta$ over all $x$.

Schematic binary loss on labels $y\in\{0,1\}$ (data vs noise):

$$
\mathcal{L}(\theta)=-\mathbb{E}\big[y\log\sigma(s_\theta(x))+(1-y)\log(1-\sigma(s_\theta(x)))\big],
$$

where $s_\theta(x)$ is a logit built from $\log u_\theta(x)-\log p_n(x)$ (plus a bias for $Z$).

### 4. Intuition

If $p_\theta$ matches $p_d$, the optimal classifier recovers the true posterior above. If $p_\theta$ is wrong, the classifier is imperfect and the loss pushes $\theta$ to fix the density ratio $p_d/p_n$.

### 5. Design choices

- **Noise $p_n$:** must overlap the data support; too far away makes the task trivial and uninformative.
- **Number of noise samples:** more noise can improve estimation but costs compute.
- NCE is a parent of later **contrastive** losses (InfoNCE) used in representation learning.

---

## Worked mini-example

Suppose data are 1D Gaussians concentrated near $0$, and noise is Uniform$[-10,10]$. A flexible $u_\theta$ that puts high mass near $0$ makes “data vs noise” easy in the right way; a flat $u_\theta$ cannot separate well. Fitting the logistic NCE loss raises $u_\theta$ where real points lie relative to $p_n$, shaping an estimated density without computing $Z$ by quadrature.

---

## Common confusions

| Confusion | Clarification |
|-----------|---------------|
| NCE needs class labels of the task | Labels are only **data vs noise**, not semantic classes. |
| Noise can be anything | Poor $p_n$ $\Rightarrow$ useless or unstable learning. |
| NCE = GANs | Related spirit (contrast), different math (explicit $p_n$, logistic NCE). |
